misconceptions.statement: Passing faeces is also excretion, the same as passing urine.
misconceptions.why: Both are 'waste leaving the body' in everyday talk.
misconceptions.fix: Faeces are undigested food that never entered the cells, so removing them is egestion. Excretion removes wastes made by the body's own cells.

probe.question: Is the removal of faeces excretion? Why?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is waste leaving the body.

misconceptions.statement: Urea is made in the kidneys.
misconceptions.why: Students see urea in urine and assume the kidney produces it, since the kidney is the organ they associate with urine.
misconceptions.fix: Urea is made in the liver from the breakdown of excess amino acids. The blood carries it to the kidneys, which filter it out.

probe.question: In which organ is urea formed?

misconceptions.root_belief: Waste is made where it is seen leaving

misconceptions.statement: Water we drink goes straight to the bladder and comes out as urine.
misconceptions.why: Students link drinking and urinating in time and think the body has a direct pipe from the stomach to the bladder.
misconceptions.fix: Water is absorbed into the blood from the gut. The kidneys then filter the blood and form urine from it. Drunk water does not go directly to the bladder.

probe.question: How does water that you drink become urine?
probe.wrong_answer: It goes from the stomach straight to the bladder

misconceptions.root_belief: Output comes straight from input without processing
misconceptions.source_hint: studies on children's ideas of the excretory system

misconceptions.statement: Blood leaves the kidney through the ureter.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up the tube that carries blood with the tube that carries urine, because both leave the kidney.
misconceptions.fix: The renal vein carries cleaned blood out of the kidney. The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

probe.question: Which tube takes blood away from the kidney after filtering?

misconceptions.root_belief: Similar-sounding tubes do the same job

misconceptions.statement: The glomerulus filters out only waste, so nothing useful leaves the blood there.
misconceptions.why: Students think the kidney is a clever filter that picks out only the wastes at once.
misconceptions.fix: The glomerulus filters out water, glucose, salts and urea together, by size and pressure. Useful substances are taken back later by reabsorption.

probe.question: What passes from the blood into the nephron at the glomerulus?

misconceptions.root_belief: Filters select only what is unwanted

misconceptions.statement: Everything that is filtered in the kidney leaves the body as urine.
misconceptions.why: Students think filtering means throwing away, so all of the filtrate must be removed.
misconceptions.fix: Most of the filtrate is reabsorbed into the blood, including all glucose, useful salts and most water. Only a small part becomes urine.

probe.question: Of the fluid filtered in the nephron, what happens to most of it?
probe.wrong_answer: All of it is passed out as urine

misconceptions.why: Students see the bladder as the place where urine is kept and where it comes out, so they think it also forms there.
misconceptions.fix: Urine is made in the kidneys. The bladder only stores it until it is passed out through the urethra.
misconceptions.root_belief: Storage organ is also the making organ
misconceptions.source_hint: studies on students' understanding of the urinary system

misconceptions.statement: Dark yellow urine means the person is healthy and has plenty of wastes removed.
misconceptions.why: Students think a stronger colour means the body is cleaning itself well.
misconceptions.fix: Dark yellow urine is more concentrated, usually because the body has too little water. Pale urine is more dilute.

probe.question: What does dark yellow urine usually show?
probe.wrong_answer: The person is very healthy and removing lots of wastes

misconceptions.root_belief: Stronger colour means better or healthier

misconceptions.statement: Sweat is only water and is not an excretion.
misconceptions.why: Students see sweat as just cooling and do not notice that it has dissolved salts and a little urea.
misconceptions.fix: Sweat contains water, salts and a little urea, so it removes some wastes. Sweating also helps cool the body.
misconceptions.root_belief: Body fluids have one simple ingredient

misconceptions.statement: Breathing out only gives back the oxygen we breathed in.
misconceptions.why: Students think the lungs only pass air in and out, so they do not see exhaled air as a waste product.
misconceptions.fix: Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide and water vapour. Carbon dioxide and water vapour are wastes of respiration removed by the lungs.

probe.question: What waste gas do the lungs remove when we breathe out?
probe.wrong_answer: None, we just breathe out the same oxygen

misconceptions.root_belief: Air breathed out is the same as breathed in
misconceptions.source_hint: research on children's ideas of breathing and respiration

misconceptions.statement: After dialysis, the patient's kidneys become healthy again.
misconceptions.why: Students see dialysis as a repair of the kidneys because the blood becomes clean.
misconceptions.fix: Dialysis cleans the blood only for a time and does not repair the kidneys. Patients need repeated dialysis or a kidney transplant.

probe.question: Does dialysis cure kidney failure?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the kidneys are repaired and work normally

misconceptions.root_belief: Treatment that helps symptoms also cures

misconceptions.statement: Kidney stones are made of the stones or sand people swallow with food or water.
misconceptions.why: Students take the word stone literally and think swallowed grit collects in the kidney.
misconceptions.fix: Kidney stones form when salts such as calcium oxalate crystallise out of urine inside the kidney. They are not swallowed grit.

probe.question: How do kidney stones form?
probe.wrong_answer: Small stones swallowed with food collect in the kidney

misconceptions.root_belief: Names of conditions describe their literal cause
